newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Generation of Sudanese children at risk - UNICEF.
newsitem.headline: Generation of Sudanese children at risk - UNICEF.

text.p: The U.N. Children's Fund (UNICEF), warning that the future of a generation of Sudanese children was at risk, appealed on Tuesday for $19 million to complete funding for its food and health programmes in the war-ravaged country.
UNICEF also urged the warring factions both to speed up efforts to end the civil conflict and to provide unconditional access to the four million women and children it is trying to assist.
The agency, which in February sought $46 million for north and southern Sudan, in June scaled back its appeal to $30.4 million due to lack of donor interest, officials said.
It has received $11.2 million so far for its Operation Lifeline Sudan but met with donors in Geneva on Tuesday to seek pledges toward the remaining $19.2 million, they added.
"I am convinced that the future of a generation of innocent children is currently at risk," Henk Franken of the Netherlands, UNICEF's representative in Khartoum, told a news briefing in Geneva.
"The effects of the conflict have spilled significantly into the north, putting children all over Sudan including the north at risk," he added. "There is no end in sight."
The rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) has been waging a 13-year civil war against Sudan's Islamist government for autonomy of the Christian and mainly animist south.
Both government troops and rebels at time have been blocking humanitarian aid, according to Franken.

A University of Khartoum study indicated between 80 and 90 per cent of the population of 26.7 million lives below the poverty line. Out of 1,000 live births, 115 children die before age five, although the toll for the south is from 180 to 200.
Child malnutrition ranges from 15 per cent in the north to 30 per cent in some areas in the south, the study found.
"Malnutrition leaves growing children mentally and physically underdeveloped while their weakened condition makes them an easy prey for various killer diseases," UNICEF said.
The aid operation was set up in April 1989 following a devastating famine in southern Sudan, resulting from drought and civil war, which killed an estimated 250,000 the previous year.
More than one million are estimated to have died since 1983 in Sudan, plagued by war for three of the last four decades. An estimated four million have been displaced by the fighting.
